correctness.rationale: For every integer k>=1, m=4k+2, pigeonhole in any correspondence yields a fiber of k+1 m-cycle vertices; a uniform packing lemma proves its diameter >= k edge steps. Hence every correspondence has distortion >=2*pi*k/m. Four contiguous blocks of sizes k+1,k,k+1,k induce a surjective square correspondence whose same/adjacent/opposite pair distance discrepancy is <=k steps, with equality inside a long block. Thus the infimum distortion equals 2*pi*k/m. Edge k=1 and wrap-around block comparisons checked; finite exhaustive tests supplement rather than replace proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full text restricts Talipov to divisible n|m or n=2,3; the geodesic square P4 and (4k+2)-gon avoid those hypotheses. Lim–Mémoli–Smith pose general p_mn and treat adjacent and circle-to-polygon cases only. Targeted literature and mathematical research-record searches did not uncover the same or a stronger exact formula; alternative chord-metric invariants do not imply this GH distance. Absolute priority remains unverified.
residual_risks: An uncatalogued recent paper or thesis may have already given this exact arithmetic family; negative search is not proof of global priority.
Later general finite-metric optimizations might imply the result without mentioning regular polygons. These were not exhaustively surveyed.

value.rationale: An exact infinite residue class of natural geometric metric spaces resolves the first source cardinality beyond equilateral simplices in a specifically posed GH-distance problem. Previous n|m results handled even targets divisible by 4, while the new nondivisible congruence class is complementary and gives the entire even-target spectrum from a geodesic square. The lower bound is a sharp cyclic packing obstruction for arbitrary multivalued correspondences, not a numerical recomputation or mere scaling.
